To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
data-dependent partitions, such as k-thresholding, nearest-neighbor partitioning and regression trees, are useful tools for constructing consistent histogram regression estimates.

(i) histogram regression estimates based upon data-dependent partitions are consistent under mild conditions, and (ii) the same conditions insure the L 2 consistency of partitioning estimates based on local polynomials.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the histogram regression estimator is consistent under very general conditions, including those for which it was previously known to be consistent.

the consistency of the histogram regression estimate is guaranteed by the following three conditions: (1) the shrinking cells, (2) the subexponential growth condition on the combinatorial complexity, and (3) the sublinear growth of the restricted cell counts.
, under the conditions of our theorem, the histogram regression estimate converges in L 2 to the regression function at a rate of O ( n - 1 / 2 ).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the histogram regression estimates are consistent if the cells shrink to a point and the combinatorial complexity of the partition grows at a rate that is slower than linear.

the histogram regression estimate based on data-dependent partitioning is L 2 -consistent if the partitioning scheme is data-dependent and satisfies the following conditions: (i) shrinking cells; (ii) subexponential growth for a combinatorial measure of complexity; (iii) sublinear growth for restricted cell counts.

, if the number of cells is allowed to grow with the number of points in a way that depends upon the smoothness and the complexity of the regression surface, the histogram regression estimates are consistent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of smoothness assumptions, the consistency of partition-based regression estimates is largely determined by the behavior of a complexity measure that counts the number of cells in a partition that contain more than a fixed number of data points.
, under general conditions, histogram regression estimates are consistent when cells are chosen to be small enough, and the number of cells is large enough.
